title: ServiceContract
description: Structural schema for a GodspeedOS service contract (`<crate>/contracts/<name>.toml`). See 13. A contract is a build-time DECLARATION: the kernel never reads it, and authority comes from the supervisor's spawn request (13.6). NOTE (2026-09-12): this schema had drifted behind the contracts it validates - six shipped services could not pass `osdev validate` because `additionalProperties: false` met four keys the schema never declared (hw_pci_class, hw_pci_bar, hw_pci_irq, pci_cfg) and an `hw_device` enum that predated the move to class-based PCI resolution. Those are added/widened here, which is permissive and so stays within v1. Two DEAD keys are deliberately NOT removed - `hw_pio` (capability retired with ATA PIO) and `spawn` (init removed, Phase 5) - because removing a key NARROWS the schema, which 13.5 makes a major version bump with a documented migration. They are marked dead in place; the narrowing is a deliberate v2, tracked in backlog/20. NOTE (2026-09-24): `console_push` was missing for the same reason and found the same way - `scripts/contract_check.py` requires any crate printing through `godspeed::io` to declare it, while `additionalProperties: false` rejected it, so the worked example the published book teaches from could not pass `osdev validate`. Added here, which is permissive and stays within v1. It went unnoticed because `osdev validate` is not run by any of the enforcement scripts - it is a separate command, and a check nobody runs is a check that is not there. NOTE (2026-10-09): the rule that note cites was false and has been reversed. `godspeed::io` prints through ConsoleWrite, which the kernel gates on LOG_WRITE alone, so `contract_check.py` now requires `log_write` of a printer and FAILS a `console_push` declaration the code never uses (see `console_push` below). The key itself stays: it is a real privilege. `osdev validate` is still on no developer build path; only the paused, workflow_dispatch-only `build.yml` runs it.

name.description: Service name. Stable identifier; used as the name-directory key.

ipc_send.description: Services this service may send IPC messages to. The send caps are minted from the spawn request's send peers; `scripts/contract_check.py` fails a service contract whose list differs from them.

ipc_receive.description: Endpoint names this service owns and may receive on.

console_push.description: Authority to push bytes into the console INPUT ring the shell reads as typed commands (privbits::CONSOLE_PUSH; 6.4 SEC-2) - the keyboard drivers' job. It is NOT needed to print: `godspeed::io` prints through ConsoleWrite, which the kernel gates on LOG_WRITE. Granted from the spawn request, like every other privilege; declared here because 13.6 makes the contract the reviewable statement of what a service may do. `scripts/contract_check.py` fails a declaration the crate's code never uses (no `console_push(` call), because an unused grant of keystroke authority is an over-grant.

log_write.description: Permission to write the kernel log: syscall 5, straight to the 16 KiB ring buffer and the serial console. NOT routed through any service - CLAUDE.md 11.4 (amendment 2026-09-04) exists to deny exactly that, so that observing a failure never depends on a service that can fail.

service_control.description: Authority to kill and restart services (privbits::SERVICE_CONTROL). Not supervisor-only: `control`, `shell` and `chaos` declare it too, and the supervisor grants it to them in their spawn rows. Reconciled against those grants by `IV-contract-authority` in scripts/commandments.py.

spawn.description: DEAD KEY. `init` was removed in Path C / Phase 5 and no contract declares this; the SPAWN privilege is carried in the supervisor's spawn REQUEST, not declared by a contract. Kept only because removing a key narrows the schema, which 13.5 makes a major version bump - see the note at the foot of this file.

hw_interrupt.description: IRQ lines the service receives, stated for REVIEW only. Nothing grants from this key and no checker reconciles it: the kernel refuses raw interrupt vectors in a spawn request and routes the interrupt of the device CLASS the request names (12.3, 14.1 amendment 2026-09-26).

hw_mmio.description: MMIO regions, base+size in hex, stated for REVIEW only. Nothing grants from this key and no checker reconciles it: the kernel refuses raw MMIO addresses in a spawn request and maps the window of the device class the request names (12.3, 14.1 amendment 2026-09-26).

hw_pio.description: DEAD KEY. The ATA-PIO block backend and the `hw_pio` capability were retired with the move to AHCI; `hw_pio` exists nowhere in kernel/ or sdk/. A contract declaring it would validate here and be unhonourable at spawn. Kept pending the v2 narrowing - see the note at the foot of this file.

hw_device.description: A NON-PCI device kind, named because nothing enumerates it: an SoC or boot fact (`dwc2` is soldered to the BCM283x, `framebuffer` is a Limine/mailbox handoff, `test-irq` is software). Each name is a lowercased SDK `hwclass::` constant; the spawn request carries that constant's number, which the kernel decodes to a `HwClass` variant. Reconciled against the `hwclass::` the supervisor's spawn row names by scripts/contract_check.py (services/ only, not examples/). `test-irq` is spelled with a hyphen and so could never match `hwclass::TEST_IRQ`; no contract uses it. PCI devices do NOT belong here - they are named by what the bus says they are, via `hw_pci_class` below (step D1). `ahci` is retained only because removing an enum member narrows the schema (13.5); nothing uses it - block-driver is `hw_pci_class = "010601"` now.

hw_pci_class.description: ANY PCI device, named by the industry-standard 24-bit (class, subclass, prog-if) triple as six hex digits - e.g. "010601" AHCI, "020000" ethernet, "0c0330" xHCI. A driver for a device this kernel has never heard of needs NO kernel change: the supervisor puts the code in the spawn request and the PCI scan answers it. The runtime BAR ADDRESS is the one fact never written down (step D1).

hw_pci_bar.description: Which BAR holds this device's registers - an INDEX (xHCI 0, AHCI 5), never an address - or "auto" for the first mapped MEMORY BAR. Belongs to the DRIVER, not the bus, which is why the contract states it.

hw_pci_irq.description: This driver takes an interrupt, so the kernel allocates a vector and programs MSI/MSI-X at spawn. Without it the driver polls. Reconciled against the supervisor's spawn row: a contract that stops declaring it while the row still asks for a vector is a FAIL, not a silent downgrade.

cpu_clock.description: Authority to set the Arm cores to the platform's minimum or maximum clock (syscall 55). Held by `power` alone, because the clock is one machine-wide setting and a second holder would silently overwrite the first; everyone else asks `power` for a lease over IPC (docs/power.md).

pci_cfg.description: Authority to READ PCI configuration space (syscall 53). Held by `hw-enumerator` alone: the kernel keeps the privileged access (x86 port I/O, the Pi 4's memory-mapped INDEX/DATA window, riscv64's flat ECAM window) and this service owns what the read MEANS - which is how bus enumeration left the kernel (step D2).

resource_mint.description: Authority to mint delegated resource capabilities - a file for fs, a socket for net-stack (§7.10, file-as-capability). Gated: granted only to services that legitimately issue resources.

core.description: Required core ID (§9.2). Omit for round-robin.
